name: Nebraska
headline_status: Medical cannabis is legal on paper after a 2024 vote, but no dispensaries are open; recreational use is illegal.
summary: Nebraska voters approved two medical cannabis initiatives in November 2024, one protecting qualified patients and one creating a regulatory commission. The Nebraska Medical Cannabis Commission has adopted restrictive rules that bar smokable flower and edibles, and as of spring 2026 no dispensaries or manufacturers were licensed and no sales had occurred. Adult-use cannabis remains illegal, though a first offense for an ounce or less is a citation with a fine.

medical_since.value: Voters approved Initiatives 437 (70.7%) and 438 (67.0%) in November 2024.

medical_program.value: Patients need a signed declaration from a licensed practitioner and may possess up to 5 ounces under Initiative 437; Commission rules prohibit raw cannabis, smokable or vaporizable products, and edibles.

retail_sales.value: None yet. As of April 2026, one of four cultivators had a variance, no manufacturers or dispensaries were licensed, and lawmakers had floated spring 2027 for first sales.

penalties.value: A first offense for 1 ounce or less is a citation with a fine of up to $300 and possible drug education; a second offense can bring up to 5 days in jail, and concentrates remain a felony.

home_grow.value: Not permitted; patients may not obtain raw cannabis under the Commission's rules.

timeline.event: Voters approve medical cannabis Initiatives 437 and 438.
Commission issues emergency rules by its statutory deadline, barring smokable cannabis and edibles.
Legislature passes its first medical cannabis bill (46-2), setting license fees and background checks.
Commission approves comprehensive regulations, sending them to the Attorney General and Governor for review.

pending.item: LB 1235, a Commission-backed bill, would add patient and practitioner registration and expand the Commission's rulemaking power.

pending.status: Awaiting Attorney General and Governor review as of April 2026.

faq.a: Recreational cannabis is illegal. Medical cannabis was approved by voters in 2024, but no dispensaries were open as of spring 2026.

faq.q: Can you buy medical marijuana in Nebraska yet?
faq.a: No. As of April 2026 no dispensaries were licensed, and officials had floated spring 2027 for first sales.
Partly. A first offense for an ounce or less is a citation with a fine of up to $300, but repeat offenses can bring jail and concentrates are a felony.
